As a Manufacturing Automation Engineer at Lexington Medical, you will design the fixtures and specify the robotics and automation equipment that build a surgical stapler, then scale those processes as production volume grows. This is an entry-level role built for an engineer coming out of school, and the work is real from the start: the fixture you design gets installed on a line that is running, and you will be on the floor when it does. Manufacturing, engineering, and quality all work in the same building in Bedford, so the loop between designing something and finding out whether it worked is short.

About Lexington Medical

Lexington Medical designs and manufactures AEON™ surgical stapling technology at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. Our products are used in minimally invasive surgery, where precision, reliability, and quality matter every time. Because engineering, manufacturing, and quality work together under one roof, the people building and supporting our products are close to both the process and the decisions behind it.

About the Role

As an Manufacturing Automation Engineer at Lexington Medical, you will support the development, implementation, and scaling of the manufacturing processes that produce our AEON™ surgical stapling products. You will design fixturing and tooling in SolidWorks, help source and commission production equipment including robotics and automation cells, provide day-to-day engineering support on the floor, and use process data to find and fix the steps that limit quality or throughput. You will work alongside experienced manufacturing engineers who will hand you real projects early rather than have you shadow theirs, and you will learn how manufacturing works inside a regulated quality system as you go.

Responsibilities

  • Design semi-automated, automated, and manual fixturing and tooling for manufacturing operations, including both digital and physical tools.
  • Work with external vendors to source custom and off-the-shelf production equipment
  • Develop and implement manufacturing processes that scale as production volume grows.
  • Provide engineering support on the production floor, troubleshooting equipment, and process issues as they come up.
  • Write and maintain manufacturing work instructions and process documentation.
  • Train production personnel on new and revised processes, and support continuous improvement and quality projects.

Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline, such as Industrial, Manufacturing, or Computer Engineering, with an expected graduation date of May or June 2027.
  • No professional experience is required. This role is open to recent graduates, and internship, co-op, or project experience designing and building mechanical or electromechanical equipment is what we look for in its place.
  • Proficient in 3D CAD, with SolidWorks preferred.
  • Coursework or hands-on experience with production methods such as machining, injection molding, or assembly processes.
  • Coursework or hands-on experience working from electrical schematics and I/O lists to wire, terminate, and troubleshoot sensors, I/O blocks, and motor control hardware at the machine or panel level.
  • Willing to spend real time on a production floor, hands-on with equipment.
  • Exposure to robotics, automation, PLCs, or motion control is a plus.
  • An internship or co-op in medical device or another regulated manufacturing environment is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

  • In your first few months, you own a fixture or tooling project from concept through installation on the line.
  • By one year, you have worked as a member of a team launching a fully automated work cell, taking responsibility for the success of a subsystem.
  • You are able to familiarize yourself with processes, equipment, and mechanisms with which you have no prior experience. You can turn this familiarity into practical, right-sized solutions on and off the production floor.

This position is based at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, in the Greater Boston area, and is an on-site role.

  • Strong communication and influencing skills

  • Demonstrated ability to lead root cause investigations, propose corrective actions & technical solutions, and execute on the implementation of those actions.

Manufacturing Engineer – Optical Systems & Sustaining Engineering

ITAR/EAR CRITERIA:

Certain positions with IDEX Corporation and its business units require access to controlled goods and technologies subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations or the Export Administration Regulations. Applicants for these positions may need to be "U.S. Persons," as defined in these regulations. Generally, a "U.S. Person" is a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, or an individual who has been granted refugee or asylum status.

About the Role

Join a team of passionate engineers dedicated to delivering next-generation healthcare technology with exceptional quality, performance, and cost-effectiveness. As part of the Manufacturing Engineering organization, you will play a critical role in transferring advanced optical technologies from concept and prototype into scalable, high-quality production environments.

This highly visible position offers the opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional teams including R&D, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Production. You will leverage your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to develop manufacturing processes, support new product introductions for successful launches, and optimize existing production systems.

Mission

The Manufacturing Engineer – Optical Systems & Sustaining Engineering serves as a key technical resource for optical and laser-based manufacturing technologies. This role supports both New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining engineering activities, contributing to the development, deployment, and continual improvement of optical systems, laser illumination

systems, and precision opto-mechanical assemblies.

The engineer will provide technical leadership in manufacturing readiness, process development, production support, troubleshooting, and workforce training while serving as a mentor and consultant to technicians and manufacturing personnel.

Position Summary

As a member of the Manufacturing Engineering team, you will be responsible for leading the development, optimization, and sustaining manufacturing processes for optical products and systems. The successful candidate will possess strong technical knowledge in one of the following: optics, lasers, or optical assemblies. A key element is an emphasis on precision

manufacturing while demonstrating the ability to rapidly learn new technologies and effectively lead the transition into

production.

This role supports multiple active product development programs and existing production lines, ensuring successful product launches, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the manufacturing value stream.

All members of the Manufacturing Engineering team are expected to embody the company's values of Team, Trust, and Excellence.

Key Responsibilities

New Product Introduction & Manufacturing Readiness

• Lead the transition of new optical and laser-based products into manufacturing.

• Implement robust manufacturing processes, work instructions, test methods, and training.

• Collaborate with R&D teams during product development to ensure manufacturability and production scalability.

• Support stage-gate development activities and manufacturing readiness reviews.

• Support qualification & validate manufacturing process and test stations prior to release.

Optical Systems Engineering

• Align and optimize optical tabletop systems and production optical assemblies.

• Support optical system integration, metrology, testing, and performance verification.

• Apply knowledge of optical principles, system tolerancing, and opto-mechanical integration.

• Support laser illumination systems, optical alignment techniques, and detector-based measurements.

• Develop fixtures, tooling, and automation to improve manufacturing efficiency and quality.

Sustaining Engineering

• Support existing products through continuous improvement, cost reduction, quality improvement, and obsolescence mitigation initiatives.

• Investigate and resolve manufacturing, supplier, and/or quality issues.

• Drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) and root cause analysis activities.

• Partner with Operations and Quality teams to improve production performance and customer satisfaction.

• Maintain technical documentation including work instructions, process specifications, and manufacturing standards.

Production Support & Continuous Improvement

• Provide technical support for production ramp activities and manufacturing operations.

• Mentor technicians and production personnel in troubleshooting, process execution, and continuous improvement.

• Identify and implement productivity improvements through Lean Manufacturing.

• Improve production throughput, yield, labor efficiency, and operational performance.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Optics, Optical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• Minimum 5 years of manufacturing engineering experience maintaining existing products and scaling up production throughput.

• Experience leading the transfer of technology from development into manufacturing.

• Experience developing manufacturing processes, documentation, and training programs.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to lead projects and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in one or more of the following areas:

• Optical assembly, alignment, and metrology

• Precision lens manufacturing and optical system production

• Laser illumination systems

• Opto-mechanical assemblies

• Optical tabletop setup and alignment

• Optical testing, detectors, and data acquisition systems

• New Product Introduction with production ramp-up and manufacturing readiness activities.

• Sustaining engineering in a production environment

Success Metrics

Performance in this position will be measured through:

• Successful on-time project execution

• Improved manufacturing readiness and production launch success

• Reduced dependency on Manufacturing Engineering and R&D after production handoff

• Effective resolution of production, supplier, and customer quality issues

• Successful scaling of manufacturing operations to support growth programs

• Development of robust manufacturing processes and technical capability within the organization

Strategic Impact

This position will directly support the organization's growth strategy by:

• Expanding manufacturing engineering capacity to support multiple development programs.

• Providing critical expertise in optics, lens manufacturing, and laser-based systems.

• Reducing single-point-of-failure risks within key technical disciplines.

• Improving manufacturing readiness and production launch performance.

• Supporting current products while enabling successful NPI execution.

• Enhancing responsiveness to customer, quality, and obsolescence-related challenges.

• Driving operational scalability as additional programs move into production.

• Enabling dedicated focus on productivity, automation, and continuous improvement initiatives.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys leading technical teams, solving complex technical challenges, working with advanced optical technologies, and building scalable manufacturing solutions that directly impact product success and organizational growth.

As the Value Chain Designer, you will help shape an integrated, resilient, and high-performing value chain for a key product group. You will manage complex supply streams, connect supplier capabilities with inventory and customer requirements, support product development value stream strategy through New Product Introduction (NPI), and turn forecast, delivery, cost, and performance data into practical improvements. This role is ideal for a supply chain leader who can see beyond individual planning activities and understand how decisions across suppliers, operations, inventory, and customer demand affect total value-chain performance.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead the development, implementation, and ongoing management of complex supply streams serving a defined product group, including streams with global reach.
  • Build an end-to-end view of the value chain by connecting supplier capacity, value stream mapping, material availability, inventory strategy, operational priorities, and customer requirements (demonstrated availability).
  • NPI value chain strategy and value chain cost strategy to meet customer expectations for product availability.
  • Manage supplier relationships and supporting processes to help ensure adequate product supply, reliable delivery, and alignment with inventory objectives.
  • Support supplier evaluation and selection by assessing value-chain capability, delivery performance, risk, quality, and operational fit.
  • Analyze supply-chain trends, sales information, forecasts, on-time delivery, inventory performance, and operational constraints to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Establish effective partnerships across operations, procurement, logistics, planning, business partners, and other internal functions to improve coordination and reduce functional silos.

What skills you will have:

Process Management: Champions continuous process improvement through governance, optimization, performance monitoring, and the adoption of best practices, tools, and methodologies.

Analytical Thinking: Applies structured analytical techniques to identify root causes, evaluate risks and opportunities, and develop data-driven solutions to complex business challenges.

Effective Communications: Effectively communicates complex information across all organizational levels, adapting messaging to the audience while influencing stakeholders and fostering collaboration.

Problem Solving: Leads the resolution of complex, high-impact business issues by organizing stakeholders, evaluating alternatives, assessing risks, and implementing sustainable solutions.

Process Mapping/Flowcharting: Utilizes advanced process mapping methodologies to document, analyze, and improve business processes while establishing organizational standards and best practices.

Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Leads structured root cause analysis efforts to identify underlying issues, implement corrective actions, prevent recurrence, and promote a culture of continuous improvement.

Job Title:                    Manufacturing Engineer

Department:               Manufacturing Engineering

Responsible for applying engineering principles and analytical techniques to establish and continuously improve manufacturing processes and products.  Functions performed may include determining the machines, equipment, and tools, as well as the sequence of operations necessary to perform production and assembly operations, recommending the design of production machines and other plant equipment, and advising and assisting vendors with design problems in connection with tools, gauges, and equipment designed for use in manufacturing.

  • High-Performance Expectations: Set and meet productivity targets to continuously improve the processes and remove costs from the business with minimal oversight and high self-awareness.
  • Sense of Urgency: Relentlessly pursue success through timely completion of capital projects and activities such as Root Cause/Corrective Action assignments in alignment with Business Unit team priorities.
  • Deal Openly and Fairly with People: Build and maintain open and honest relationships with Manufacturing Engineering teammates and cross functional teammates from Quality Engineering, Product Engineering, and Manufacturing Operations.
  • Bias for Action: Proactively address manufacturing opportunities with a strong focus on Safety, Quality and Delivery.
  • Open and Honest Communication: Foster transparency by proactively sharing relevant information, actively listening to stakeholders, and addressing challenges with clarity and integrity.

 

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES/COMPETENCIES

 

  • Problem Solving: Handle day-to-day problems with processes, product, equipment and documentation.  Investigate and complete assigned Corrective Action Requests, working with assigned Business Unit team to systematically identify and address root cause. Assist and coordinate with maintenance and facility engineering for process and equipment troubleshooting to support production goals and reduce downtime.
  • Productivity Improvements: Identify and address areas of productivity (i.e. scrap, downtime, effectiveness) improvement using systematic problem solving and Lean Manufacturing techniques.
  • Capital Projects: Identify, properly scope, manage and implement Capital Investment projects to improve productivity (i.e. scrap, downtime, effectiveness).

  • Technical Communication: Compose and process documentation and process changes using the Engineering Change Requests (ECR) procedure.
  • Cross-Functional Teamwork: Actively participate and represent Manufacturing Engineering in new product design reviews.  Interact, when required, with customers during audits, product investigations and presentations.

 

 

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering field (Mechanical preferred) with strong problem solving skills
  • Minimum five (5) years related experience, preferably in Aerospace or Automotive environment
  • Experience with metal-joining processes (Tig, resistance welding, brazing) preferred
  • Solidworks (preferred)
  • Experience with robot/cobot automation
  • Capital Project Management ($2,500 - $1.5M)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 

The employee is expected to adhere to all company policies.

We’re Hiring: Manufacturing Engineer I


Are you a hands-on engineer who enjoys turning ideas into practical improvements on the production floor? Kato Cable is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer I to help improve the efficiency, quality, and consistency of our manufacturing processes.

In this role, you will work closely with Production, Quality, Project Engineering, and Supply Chain to:

  • Support customer-driven manufacturing projects from setup through production
  • Design and implement tooling, fixtures, and jigs
  • Develop and improve work instructions, SOPs, and testing requirements
  • Support new product introductions and production-line readiness
  • Troubleshoot equipment, tooling, material, and process issues
  • Use Lean Manufacturing and 5S principles to reduce waste and improve workflow
  • Help ensure manufacturing changes are properly documented and implemented

This is an excellent opportunity for an engineer who wants to be actively involved in manufacturing—not sitting behind a desk all day. You’ll spend meaningful time on the production floor, learn our processes firsthand, and help create solutions that make a measurable difference.

 

Schedule: Monday - Thursday, 5:30 am - 4:00 pm
Salary: $ 65,000 - $ 75,000 annually


What we’re looking for:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
  • A self-driven, hands-on approach to problem-solving
  • Strong planning, documentation, and communication skills
  • Willingness to learn production processes through direct, hands-on experience
  • Basic CAD and Microsoft Office skills
  • Manufacturing, wire harness, cable assembly, Lean, Six Sigma, or ERP experience is preferred

If you are driven by continuous improvement, committed to quality, and ready to grow your engineering career with a collaborative manufacturing team, we would love to hear from you.


Apply today!


Kato Cable is located in Mankato, Minnesota.


Requirements

 JOB PURPOSE: The Manufacturing Engineer I supports manufacturing operations by applying engineering principles within a designated production area and assisting with customer-driven projects. This role focuses on improving production efficiency, quality, and consistency through effective documentation, equipment setup and optimization, and continuous improvement initiatives. The Manufacturing Engineer I works closely with cross-functional teams to support safe, compliant, and efficient manufacturing processes.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop proficiency in one of three designated production areas within an established onboarding and training period and provide ongoing engineering support within that area.
  • Support and execute customer-driven manufacturing projects by ensuring tooling, testing, and manufacturing processes are established, documented, and maintained throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Design and support the implementation of tooling, fixtures, and jigs to improve productivity, quality, and repeatability.
  • Assist in the development, maintenance, and improvement of work instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs), fixtures, and testing requirements.
  • Support equipment setup, documentation, and optimization while ensuring compliance with customer specifications, quality standards, and internal procedures.
  • Analyze production workflows and assist production teams with continuous improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing and 5S principles to reduce waste, improve efficiency, and minimize process variation.
  • Execute Engineering Change Orders (ECOs), Design Review Forms (DRFs), and Process Improvement Forms (PIFs) to ensure accurate documentation, proper approvals, and effective implementation of manufacturing changes.
  • Assist with troubleshooting basic issues related to equipment, tooling, fixtures, materials, and manufacturing processes.
  • Participate in New Product Introduction (NPI) activities, including documentation development, line readiness, and process validation.
  • Collaborate effectively with Production, Quality, Project Engineering, and Supply Chain teams to support manufacturing goals and customer requirements.
  • Apply independent judgment and engineering fundamentals to evaluate manufacturing processes and recommend improvements under the guidance of senior engineering staff.

In addition, this role may be assigned other duties consistent with the nature and level of the position, as required to support ongoing business needs.
QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience, Competencies and Education
  • Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering field required.
  • Willingness to work on the production floor and learn through hands-on tasks.
  • Language Skills

Ability to read, analyze and interpret technical documents, work instructions, specifications, and procedures relevant to the role.  

  • Mathematical Skills

Ability to perform basic mathematical equations relevant to manufacturing and engineering tasks. 

  • Reasoning Ability

Ability to manage a variety of job assignments, apply logical reasoning, and solve routine manufacturing-related problems with guidance as needed. 
REQUIRED COMPUTER SKILLS

  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft Outlook
  • Basic CAD software
  • General internet and computer use

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

  • Previous experience in a manufacturing or production environment preferred.
  • Three to five years of cable assembly/wire harness experience.  
  • Exposure to Lean Manufacturing principles or Six Sigma methodologies.
  • Experience with ERP systems or basic manufacturing- related data entry.

ACCOUNTABILITIES AND MEASURES

  • Timely and accurate completion of assigned engineering tasks and project deliverables.
  • Adherence to the Company Quality Policy and ISO procedural requirements.
  • Compliance with safety policies, housekeeping standards, and good manufacturing practices.
  • Ability to work independently, follow established work rules, remain flexible, and perform a variety of engineering support tasks as required.
  • Ability to safely operate and support manufacturing equipment as necessary to perform engineering and production support duties.
  • Ability to work effectively, courteously, and respectfully with all levels of personnel.

Vision Requirements

  • Close vision (clear vision at 20 inches or less)
  • Distance vision (clear vision at 20 feet or more)
  • Color vision (ability to identify and distinguish colors)
  • Peripheral vision (ability to observe an area that can be seen up and down or to the left and right while eyes are fixed on a given point)
  • Depth perception (three-dimensional vision, ability to judge distances and spatial relationships)
